correctness.rationale: For every two-type prefix, the parity-compatible unit-count split exactly minimizes load discrepancy; the proof handles parity-perfect partitions and insufficient small goods separately. For r=2,3, a small arrival preserves the split without transfers and a large arrival uses at most one unit-good transfer, with an explicit itemwise upgrade injection. The five-good history of four units then one item r>=4 requires changing a 2-good bundle to a singleton, violating the injection cardinality constraint. A standalone enumerator checked 458752 positive-case prefixes and the obstruction for r=4..30; infinite validity rests on the algebraic induction, not the finite counts.

value.rationale: Standardized resource sizes are a natural restriction in dynamic fair allocation and two-machine load covering. The theorem resolves exact MMS feasibility under the substantive itemwise nonworsening restriction at each arrival, with a simple sharp 3-versus-4 integer ratio and a deterministic constant-time update requiring at most one relocation. Its five-good obstruction isolates the resource-size reason for incompatibility, rather than merely repeating the general constant-factor guarantee.
